description: Main window: read/write the app-data workspace; native dialogs for import/export; clipboard for copy actions. Programs (pandoc, Diogenes' perl exporter, the AI CLIs) run only through the app's own job commands in src-tauri/src/commands.rs, which take no program path or argv from the window — the window names a job and supplies data (workbench-design/sandboxing-plan.md); app commands need no capability entry beyond core:default. The fs:allow-exists scope covers onboarding's existence checks only (Diogenes install location and the user-picked TLG folder). The broader read/write/mkdir/read-dir/stat '/**' scopes support a user-picked library folder (shared-folder sync, build spec §11) — the folder is chosen explicitly via the native picker, same trust model as the TLG folder. fs:allow-remove is what "Remove work" needs (src/lib/library/storage.ts): it deletes one work's own folder under the library root, recursively, after the work has been dropped from works.json. Its scope matches the write-text-file and mkdir grants already present — the library root is a folder the user picks through the native picker, and an app that may overwrite any file in it could already destroy the same content. core:window:allow-destroy is what the close button needs (src/App.svelte): the close handler saves every open editor first, then the window destroys itself. fs:allow-rename is what saves need (src/lib/library/storage.ts, settings.ts): every chapter file, works.json and settings.json is written to a temp file beside it and renamed into place, so a crash mid-write cannot truncate a translation. Its scope matches the write-text-file grant. fs:allow-read-file is what the TLG/PHI importer needs and is NOT implied by fs:allow-read: 'read' is the byte-range command on an open handle, 'read_file' slurps a whole file, and AUTHTAB.DIR and the .IDT indexes are binary, so read-text-file cannot serve them. Its scope matches the read-text-file grant already present. The open/read/seek entries exist for Latin lookup: Diogenes' latin-analyses.txt is ~43MB and must be read by byte range through its companion index rather than slurped whole (src/lib/lexicon/latinAnalyses.ts), and the existing read-text-file/stat scopes are whole-file only. Their '/**' scope matches the read-text-file grant already present — the file being read is the user's own Diogenes install, whose location the user sets. opener:allow-reveal-item-in-dir is what 'Reveal in Finder' after an export needs; it was never granted, so the reveal failed silently.
